headline: High: AutoGen’s writable, executable default surfaces can conflict with a non-runnable reference list, while prompt-injection and leakage risks are otherwise limited by B’s lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, so if its outputs are manually copied into the other profile’s workflow, malicious instructions could be propagated. The awesome-production-machine-learning profile is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so there is no direct machine-to-machine channel; the pathway is only via operator bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies AutoGen-generated text into a downstream agent prompt or task queue
IF the downstream workflow treats copied content as instructions without review
mitigations: Use a human review step before reusing AutoGen output
Strip code blocks and imperative language before forwarding
Keep the reference-list agent read-only and non-runnable
Separate chat transcripts from task inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can touch application data and model-provider API keys, but the second profile is a non-runnable awesome list with no I/O surfaces or data classes touched. With no shared workspace or outbound path on B, leakage is limited to whatever the operator manually transfers from A into B’s context.
conditions: IF AutoGen is configured to process sensitive application data in its working directory
IF an operator manually pastes that data into another system
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in AutoGen working directories
Use separate folders per task
Redact sensitive fields before sharing outputs
Keep the reference-list agent offline and read-only
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and configurable shared-state behavior; the other profile is non-runnable, so it cannot contend for resources itself. The conflict risk is therefore mostly one-sided contention around shared directories or state if the operator wires B into the same workspace, which is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF AutoGen instances are pointed at the same writable directory
IF external tooling wraps the reference list into a mutable shared workspace
mitigations: Assign unique working directories per run
Disable shared-state reuse between instances
Avoid concurrent writes to the same git or cache path
Run AutoGen in Docker isolation when possible
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate tool calls and code, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. The second profile is only a static reference list, so it will not itself act on A’s output; however, if an operator uses A’s generated facts to update or curate B, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream work products.
conditions: IF AutoGen output is used as source material for curation or automation
IF no verification step checks the generated facts before reuse
mitigations: Require a verification pass before reuse
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted drafts
Compare generated claims against primary sources
Keep B as a static curated list, not an action agent
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data, while the second profile is a non-runnable public reference list with no data classes touched. There is no documented residency or certification mismatch between them, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive data inside AutoGen’s workspace rather than a pairwise policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into AutoGen’s working directory
IF the operator republishes that data into a separate system with stricter policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AutoGen runs
Use synthetic or masked inputs
Document data-handling boundaries
Store outputs in a separate non-sensitive folder
requires-engineering: map residency and retention policies
